In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the form factor of the vortex lattice is not a constant, but a function of the field.
the paramagnetic effects in CeCoIn5 are not strong enough to suppress the superconductivity.

the vortex lattice in the paramagnetic limit is not a simple hexagonal structure, but a complex one with a large anisotropy and with the form factor varying from one vortex to another, depending on the vortex lattice orientation with respect to the crystal axis and on the vortex position inside the unit cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the paramagnetism of the normal electrons is the key for the understanding of the vortex lattice of unconventional superconductors.
the paramagnetic effects are not negligible for the description of the vortex lattice in CeCoIn5 and the vortex lattice is not a perfect square.
in the case of CeCoIn_ 5, where the paramagnetic effects are important, the form factor of the Abrikosova lattice is not a constant, as was previously assumed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the paramagnetic contribution to superconducting currents can be important in the vicinity of H_c2 and should be taken into account in the analysis of the magnetic response in the mixed state.
the paramagnetic effects in the vortex lattice of unconventional superconductors are very strong and cannot be ignored.
the paramagnetic contribution to the superfluid current is not negligible in the case of CeCoIn_ 5, even at the approach of the upper critical field.
